transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-15
Start: 14:30 PST
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Sofia (Redwood AE), Devon (Redwood SE), Maya (Redwood SE), Aarav (Rivermark ML), Lena (Rivermark Platform), Tom (Rivermark CTO)
Links shared: https://drive.google.com/rm-benchmark-template (benchmark template), https://rdrm.internal/samples/rivermark_samp_requests.csv (customer sample placeholder)

00:00 Sofia: okay hey everyone thanks for joining, um uh quick roll call, we got Rivermark folks?
00:06 Aarav: yeah aarav here, lena and tom on, thanks for coordinating
00:09 Sofia: great, quick agenda — define success criteria for the POC, gather workload signals (qps, concurrency, token mix), agree benchmark methodology and timeline. Is that fair?
00:16 Tom: yep that's what we need, we're trying to validate cost/perf tradeoffs before committing to dedicated capacity
00:22 Devon: perfect; can i start by asking about observed qps and burst profiles? specifically peak sustained qps and episodic bursts — like 1 minute, 5 minute, 15 minute windows?
00:30 Aarav: so our production is kinda spiky, we run banking assistant flows — baseline qps is around 30 qps but we see bursts to 1.1k qps during statement run windows, usually 2–3 minutes long, occasionally longer on payroll days
00:44 Maya: mm-hmm, and concurrency — are bursts single-user multi-turn sessions or lots of single-turn calls?
00:50 Aarav: mixture — the onboarding flow is multi-turn, average session concurrency per user is 3–5 steps, but 80% of the burst is many single-turn checks (balance inquiries). so the token distribution changes: bursts are short inputs, short outputs; other times we have long generative flows for account analysis with outputs 200–600 tokens
01:10 Devon: good detail. do you have token histograms? median input, median output, 95th percentiles? even ballpark numbers help sizing
01:18 Aarav: rough numbers — input median ~40 tokens, output median ~150 tokens, p95 output ~420 tokens, p99 rare runs up to 2k tokens for report generation but those are 0.1% of traffic
01:30 Lena: also important — we have top 12 routes that account for 94% of traffic, most sensitive are balance-check and transaction-history retrievals
01:38 Sofia: sounds typical of financial workloads; success criteria we usually propose: p95 latency <= 350ms for short flows (<=200 output tokens) under production bursts, and p99 tail observed but can be higher for the long-report jobs. Is p95 <= 350ms acceptable?
01:50 Tom: that would be good — ideally 300 but we can cap at 350 for POC. Cost target: under $0.70 per 1k output tokens across mixed workload — ballpark
01:59 Devon: okay we'll model both latency SLO and unit cost. couple questions about data residency and deployment mode — are you planning Redwood Private in your VPC or hosted?
02:08 Lena: we need VPC/private for PII reasons. we'll want a private control plane or at least customer-managed keys; KMS integration mandatory. SOC2 is table stakes
02:16 Sofia: noted. we'll include Private deployment notes and KMS integration in the security pack.
02:20 Aarav: for benchmarks, do you recommend synthetic replay or live shadowing? we can do sanitized logs, but not sure about real traffic replays for security
02:28 Devon: both have pros/cons. synthetic replay is safe and reproducible — we seed with your sampled requests and scale qps to match bursts. live shadowing gives most realism but needs network controls. for initial sizing we propose synthetic replay using your sample corpus, then a live replay in VPC if sandbox access is available
02:47 Maya: also want to instrument KV cache effects — some flows benefit massively from prefix caching; we should capture session overlap patterns so we can simulate cache hit rate (e.g., expected KV hit 22% in your baseline)
03:00 Aarav: we see approx 20–25% prefix reuse on balance queries, but for analytics flows reuse is nearly zero
03:06 Devon: okay we'll parameterize cache hit rate in the benchmark. on the runtime side we'll test a few knobs: batch size, continuous batching windows, kv cache enabled/disabled, and quantized model variants.
03:16 Sofia: what's your tolerance for small accuracy regressions from quantized models?
03:20 Tom: not much for transaction summaries; for simple balance checks it's fine. we'll include an eval set to validate quality — we can fail the POC if summaries degrade beyond X% metric — we'll define that in the acceptance criteria
03:32 Devon: good. for acceptance metrics we'll propose: (1) p95 latency <= 350ms for short flows at peak burst QPS, (2) sustained throughput across a 5-minute burst with less than 5% request failures, (3) unit cost <= $0.70 per 1k output tokens, (4) no PII leakage and successful KMS integration/workflow.
03:52 Aarav: sounds right. how do you define "short flows"?
03:56 Devon: short flows: outputs <= 200 tokens and inputs <= 100 tokens. long flows defined separately for p99 analysis.
04:03 Lena: about metrics: we need token-level accounting per route and per-token cost breakdowns, can Redwood Console provide that?
04:09 Maya: yes console gives token-level cost breakdown, per-route dashboards, and latency percentiles per model variant. we'll add tracing hooks so you can map requests to infra traces
04:20 Tom: okay, timeline — how long to run a POC?
04:23 Sofia: typically 3–4 weeks: week 0 prep and corpus collection, week 1 synthetic replay and preliminary sizing, week 2 live replay/validation in VPC + tuning, week 3 analysis & playbook handoff. If you want longer we can extend but that's the typical cadence
04:36 Aarav: what's needed from our side now?
04:39 Sofia: a sanitized sample request corpus (~2 weeks) with route labels, top 20 routes, token counts, and expected traffic cadence. also your acceptance thresholds in writing (we'll draft).
04:49 Aarav: i can get that by thursday 12/17, we'll redact account numbers and names
04:53 Devon: perfect. meanwhile we'll create a sizing workbook — we'll include lanes for baseline, 95th percentile bursts, and extreme payroll-day bursts. we'll model concurrency assuming mix of multi-turn and single-turn flows.
05:07 Maya: curious — do you have recommended synthetic scaling patterns? like Poisson vs fixed bursts?
05:12 Devon: we typically run a two-phase pattern: baseline Poisson at measured mean for 20 minutes, then injected bursts with step increases to peak sustained qps for configured windows (1, 3, 5 minutes) and microbursts (10–20s) to stress tail latencies.
05:26 Tom: okay, make sure you capture cold-start impacts and kv cache warmup; our lambda-style flows see cold token cache on first run each day
05:35 Devon: noted, we'll do cold-to-warm ramps and measure warm steady-state separately. also we'll surface KV cache hit traces so you can see improvements
05:42 Sofia: pricing: we'll include a scoping estimate for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. since you need VPC, likely private licensing + infra; we'll show marginal cost per 1k tokens across the variants
05:55 Aarav: and fallback model strategies — if the big model can't meet latency during bursts can Redwood route to a smaller quantized model automatically?
06:02 Maya: yes, we have smart routing and automatic fallback to compatible variants — we can simulate that during the benchmark and measure quality drop and latency improvement
06:11 Devon: final bits — we'll need an eval harness (we can provide a small python runner) to score summaries for quality regressions. can you provide the reference oracle dataset?
06:18 Tom: yes we'll produce an eval set for the summary route, about 250 labeled cases
06:22 Sofia: great. any other constraints?
06:24 Lena: security: KMS integration, VPC peering, audit logs retention — we'll need options for 7yr audit logs eventually but POC should demonstrate log export to our logging stack
06:35 Sofia: we'll add log export and KMS notes to the security pack.
06:38 Aarav: good. so recap?
06:40 Sofia: recap: Rivermark to provide sanitized sample corpus + eval set by 2026-12-17; Redwood to share benchmark template and sizing workbook by 12/17; live replay scheduled week of 12/21; acceptance criteria: p95 <= 350ms on short flows, unit cost ceiling $0.70/1k output tokens, failure rate <5% on bursts, and KMS + no PII leakage.
06:58 Tom: agreed. thanks all.
07:00 Sofia: i'll send notes and next steps, Devon will share sizing workbook. thanks everyone
07:04 Meeting end.

Notes on transcription quality: occasional mis-heard acronyms (kay vee cache, Redwood Privatee), some speaker swaps near the end when call connection had minor glitch.

Artifacts referenced:
- Benchmark template: https://drive.google.com/rm-benchmark-template
- Placeholder sample corpus (customer to upload sanitized): rivermark_samp_requests.csv
- Proposed sizing workbook (to be sent): rm_qps_concurrency_model_Devon.xlsx

Acceptance criteria (plain text):
- p95 latency <= 350ms for short flows (outputs <= 200 tokens) under production burst profile
- p99 latency documented and characterized for long jobs (>200 tokens) but not a strict gate
- Sustained 5-minute burst throughput with <5% failures
- Unit cost <= $0.70 per 1k output tokens across mixed workload
- KMS integration demonstrated and no PII leakage in any test

"End of transcript"
